NASA's Voyager 1 spacecraft was due to reach one light-day from Earth on 18 November, about 26 billion kilometres away, according to NASA and Space.com. At that distance a radio signal takes 24 hours to travel each way, so a command and its reply take two days.

Space.com said the milestone was expected at 10:16 GMT, or 9:16pm AEDT. Voyager 1 launched in September 1977 and in 2012 became the first human-made spacecraft to enter interstellar space, NASA said. It travels at about 61,000km/h. Its twin, Voyager 2, is expected to reach the same distance in November 2035, according to Space.com.
keyFacts: One light-day is about 26 billion kilometres
Signals take 24 hours each way
Voyager 2 is expected to reach the mark in 2035

articles.title: Woolworths plans 100 to 125 new supermarkets over five years
articles.summary:
Woolworths plans to open 20 to 25 new stores a year over the next three to five years, adding 100 to 125 supermarkets over five years, AAP reported. The company opened 127 stores in the past decade.

Chief executive Amanda Bardwell told an investor briefing on Wednesday that new stores support the company's online growth, according to AAP. About two-thirds of its 1,130 Australian supermarkets have been renewed, and 60 to 85 more will be refitted each year. AAP said scan-and-go trolleys are in 100 stores, with a wider rollout planned before Christmas.
keyFacts: Woolworths has 1,130 Australian supermarkets
It plans 20 to 25 openings a year
It opened 127 stores in the past decade

articles.title: Wife of Melbourne activist held in Vietnam urges stronger push for his release
articles.summary:
The wife of Melbourne activist Tran Hiep, who has been detained in Vietnam since September, has urged the federal government to press harder for his release, AAP reported. Vietnamese authorities say he is accused of terrorism and forging documents; he was taken from Cambodia.

Prime Minister Anthony Albanese raised the case with Vietnam's prime minister at the ASEAN summit on Sunday, according to AAP. Chloe Dang welcomed that but said her husband's case should not be treated like criminal cases. His lawyer said normal diplomacy was not working. Vietnamese authorities said detained men admitted membership of Viet Tan, which Vietnam lists as a terrorist group. A consular visit is set for 20 November.
keyFacts: Tran Hiep, 51, is held in Ho Chi Minh City
Albanese raised the case at the ASEAN summit
A consular visit is scheduled for 20 November

articles.title: Rubio says no evidence recent US outages were caused by a hostile actor
articles.summary:
US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said there was zero evidence that recent outages affecting Microsoft, the Federal Aviation Administration, JPMorgan Chase and the National Security Agency were linked or caused by rival countries or criminals, AP reported.

The outages have disrupted US flights, business services and the NSA's classified internal network in recent days. The NSA has attributed its outage to routine maintenance, and Microsoft said its outage was caused by an earlier network capacity upgrade. Rubio made the comments while travelling with President Donald Trump in Asia, according to AP.
keyFacts: Rubio cited outages at four organisations
He said there was no sign of a malign actor
The NSA blamed its outage on maintenance

articles.title: Russian strike on Kryvyi Rih kills two and wounds 60, officials say
articles.summary:
A Russian attack on Kryvyi Rih, President Volodymyr Zelenskiy's hometown, killed a seven-year-old boy and a 20-year-old woman on Friday night, city administration head Oleksandr Vilkul said. Regional officials said 60 people were wounded, including six children.

Vilkul said about 25 apartment buildings, a hospital, schools and an industrial site were damaged, and that later missiles struck rescuers and utility crews, according to Al Jazeera, citing AFP and AP. Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk described Friday's landing of Russian missiles in Poland as a deliberate provocation. Russian authorities said a Ukrainian attack in Luhansk killed six people; that claim has not been independently verified.
keyFacts: Officials said a boy, 7, and a woman, 20, were killed
60 people were wounded, including six children, officials said
About 25 apartment buildings and a hospital were damaged, Vilkul said

articles.title: COP31 talks stay deadlocked as EU signals it could walk away over fossil fuel wording
articles.summary:
Climate talks at COP31 in Antalya went into an extra day on Saturday with no agreement on whether the final text should refer to fossil fuels, RTÉ and The Irish Times reported. The new development is that the EU is understood to be prepared to walk away rather than accept weak wording, according to The Irish Times, and a third draft due on Saturday morning had not appeared by lunchtime.

RTÉ said Saudi Arabia and its allies oppose the EU's preferred wording, while Panama has said it will not accept a text that omits fossil fuels. Negotiations chair Chris Bowen said he still believed a deal was possible. Any agreement requires consensus.
keyFacts: Talks ran into an extra day on Saturday without a deal
The Irish Times said the EU is prepared to walk away rather than accept weak text
Panama said it will block a text without fossil fuel wording, RTÉ reported

articles.title: Mexico captures alleged cartel leader 'El Chapo Isidro', on FBI's most wanted list
articles.summary:
Mexico's National Defence Secretariat said special forces captured Fausto Isidro Meza-Flores, known as "Chapo Isidro", in a raid in Sinaloa state on Friday night local time, along with two other gang leaders. The FBI lists him among its ten most wanted fugitives and alleges he leads a group that trafficked heroin, methamphetamine, cocaine, fentanyl and marijuana into the US.

The Mexican government said US intelligence assisted, without giving details, according to the ABC, citing AFP and AP. CBS News reported violence in Sinaloa after the arrest, including gunfire near a baseball game in Guasave. Meza-Flores faces charges in Mexico and the US, where a reward of up to $US5 million had been offered.
keyFacts: Mexico's defence ministry announced the capture in Sinaloa
The FBI lists Meza-Flores among its ten most wanted
CBS reported violence in Sinaloa after the arrest

articles.title: Trump says he will work with Democrats to cap credit card interest at 10%
articles.summary:
US President Donald Trump said on Saturday he would work with the incoming Democrat-controlled Congress to cap credit card interest rates at 10 per cent, telling Fox News Channel he would do it, according to AP. Senator Elizabeth Warren, expected to chair the Senate Banking Committee, has said she supports a cap.

Trump proposed the cap in January, and banks opposed it, warning that cards could be cancelled or rewards cut, AP reported. An August New York Fed survey put the median card rate at about 22.2 per cent. Consumer Financial Protection Bureau figures show about 195 million Americans held cards in 2024 and paid $US160 billion in interest.
keyFacts: Trump backed a 10% cap in a Fox News interview on Saturday
Banks have opposed the proposal, AP reported
The median US card rate is about 22.2%, New York Fed data show

articles.title: FBI national crime database suffers suspected breach, US media report
articles.summary:
The FBI's National Crime Information Center, which police use to share warrant and background-check information, has suffered a suspected breach, CNN and NBC reported on Friday, citing two people briefed on the matter, according to Al Jazeera. NBC separately reported an apparent cyberattack on the US Department of Agriculture.

President Donald Trump appeared to confirm the FBI hack in a television interview on Saturday, saying it was "not good", Al Jazeera reported. The FBI and the Agriculture Department did not immediately respond to requests for comment, and FBI Director Kash Patel has not commented publicly. The breach has not been officially confirmed by the bureau.
keyFacts: CNN and NBC reported a suspected breach of the FBI's NCIC system
Trump appeared to confirm the hack in a Saturday interview
The FBI has not officially confirmed the breach

articles.title: US judge approves Bayer's $US7.25 billion Roundup cancer settlement
articles.summary:
A St Louis judge on Friday approved a settlement under which Bayer will pay up to $US7.25 billion over as long as 21 years to resolve claims that its Roundup weedkiller caused non-Hodgkin lymphoma, AP reported. Circuit Judge Timothy Boyer described the payouts as fair and adequate in a written order.

AP said participants could receive on average between $US10,000 and $US165,000, depending on factors including exposure and illness severity. Bayer denies that Roundup causes cancer, and its chief executive Bill Anderson called the settlement a milestone. Some plaintiffs' lawyers say the payments are too small, and the approval could be appealed. The cancer link remains disputed between the WHO's cancer agency and the US EPA.
keyFacts: The settlement is worth up to $US7.25 billion over 21 years
Bayer denies Roundup causes cancer
The approval can still be appealed, AP reported

articles.title: US jury finds man guilty of starting fire that became deadly Palisades blaze
articles.summary:
A federal jury in Los Angeles on Friday found Jonathan Rinderknecht guilty of arson-related charges over the fire that grew into the January 2025 Palisades Fire, NBC Los Angeles and ABC7 reported. Prosecutors alleged he started the Lachman Fire on New Year's Day 2025, which rekindled days later in strong winds. The Palisades Fire killed 12 people and destroyed thousands of structures.

It was a retrial; the first trial ended in a mistrial in June with jurors split 10-2 in favour of acquittal. Prosecutors cited phone location data and online search records. His lawyer, Steve Haney, argued the evidence was circumstantial and that fireworks could have caused the blaze. Sentencing is set for March 2027.
keyFacts: Rinderknecht was found guilty at a retrial on Friday
His first trial ended in a 10-2 mistrial in June
Sentencing is set for 17 March 2027

articles.title: New national rules for home birth midwives take effect in January
articles.summary:
From January, every midwife attending a home birth must hold an endorsement requiring extra training and 5,000 hours of work to qualify for professional indemnity insurance, AAP reported. Secondary midwives were previously exempt, and two midwives are required at a home birth.

The federal government says the change makes home birth safer and closes insurance gaps. Midwives and mothers say it could halve the number of home births, and rallies were planned around Australia on Saturday. Senators from several parties have asked Assistant Health Minister Rebecca White to reverse the change. White said the decision was made more than 18 months ago and that public home birth services remain unchanged.
keyFacts: The rules apply to all home birth midwives from January
Opponents say home births could fall by half or more
White said public home birth services are unchanged

articles.title: US sanctions Comancheros bikie club leaders over alleged cartel links
articles.summary:
The US Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control has sanctioned the Australia-headquartered Comancheros motorcycle club and Italy's 'Ndrangheta, saying both run transnational criminal networks, AAP and 1News reported. Those named include Allan Meehan, described by AAP as the club's alleged "world president", and New Zealand chapter leaders.

OFAC alleged the Comancheros facilitated large cocaine shipments. The sanctions block US-held property and bar dealings with those listed. Australian Federal Police Assistant Commissioner Stephen Nutt said members could lose access to banking. AAP said Australia does not enforce US sanctions, but local businesses may need to consider them. OFAC worked with the AFP and New Zealand Police.
keyFacts: OFAC sanctioned the Comancheros and the 'Ndrangheta
Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent approved the sanctions on 19 November, AAP said
The AFP and NZ Police assisted, according to 1News

articles.title: Victorian Labor pledges health funding as parties dispute VicHealth's future
articles.summary:
Victorian Premier Ben Carroll pledged $14.4 million so emergency patient transport staff can transfer long service leave, and said Labor would keep 132 nursing positions at Werribee Mercy Hospital, AAP reported. Carroll said the Coalition would make large cuts and One Nation wants to privatise hospitals; both parties' positions on those claims were not reported.

The parties also differ on VicHealth, which the government plans to merge into the Department of Health after a December review. Opposition Leader Jess Wilson has committed to keeping it independent, a position backed by the Public Health Association and the AMA, AAP said. One Nation's Barnaby Joyce said the party faced a difficult task. Victorians vote on 28 November.
keyFacts: Labor pledged $14.4m for patient transport staff leave
Labor plans to absorb VicHealth; Wilson pledges to keep it independent
The state election is on 28 November

articles.title: Malaysia says it will resettle 10,000 Rohingya refugees in Turkey
articles.summary:
Malaysian Deputy Prime Minister Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said on Friday that Malaysia will resettle 10,000 Rohingya refugees in Turkey through a skills training program, AAP reported. He said the government would work with Turkish authorities and the UN refugee agency and would consider the consent of those involved. Turkey's foreign ministry did not immediately respond.

The announcement came a day after the International Court of Justice ruled Myanmar committed genocide against the Rohingya. A Myanmar government spokeswoman called the ruling unfair and said it was a nine-to-six decision. UNHCR figures show Malaysia had about 193,000 registered refugees from Myanmar at the end of February.
keyFacts: Malaysia plans to resettle 10,000 Rohingya in Turkey
Turkey had not responded, AAP reported
Myanmar called the ICJ genocide ruling unfair

articles.title: Honda and Toyota recall 1.6 million US vehicles over Takata airbag risk
articles.summary:
Honda and Toyota are recalling about 1.6 million vehicles in the US because their Takata airbag inflators could rupture, the ABC reported, citing Reuters. Both companies said no injuries, crashes or ruptures have been linked to the recalled vehicles.

The US road safety regulator NHTSA said the companies saw early evidence of degradation risk. Honda's recall covers 810,592 older US vehicles, while Toyota's covers 790,000 vehicles worldwide, including 314,000 in the US. Inflators will be replaced. Defective Takata inflators have been linked to at least 28 US deaths since 2009. Lexus has also recalled more than 7,000 vehicles in Australia, the ABC said.
keyFacts: About 1.6 million US vehicles are being recalled
The companies said no injuries are linked to these vehicles
Lexus has recalled more than 7,000 vehicles in Australia

articles.title: Fire at Iraqi power station near Basra kills at least four
articles.summary:
A fire at the Hartha power station north of Basra killed at least four people and injured 35, according to the Iraqi News Agency, as reported by Al Jazeera on Saturday. The civil defence directorate said the blaze at the station and nearby houses had been brought under control.

Operations at the 800-megawatt plant were halted, the agency said. The cause has not been confirmed. Footage shared online showed smoke and burnt-out cars near the site, according to Al Jazeera. Iraq's electricity grid has faced long-running shortfalls, and previous substation fires have caused power cuts in the country.
keyFacts: At least four people died and 35 were injured, state media said
The 800-megawatt Hartha station was shut down
The cause of the fire has not been confirmed

articles.title: India's Congress youth wing protests at Meta offices over account restrictions
articles.summary:
The youth wing of India's opposition Congress party protested outside Meta offices in Hyderabad, Mumbai and Gurugram on Friday, according to Al Jazeera, citing Anadolu and Reuters. In Hyderabad, protesters entered the building and scuffled with police. The party alleges Meta restricted Instagram accounts of its leaders on 19 November at the request of the ruling BJP.

BJP spokesperson Pradeep Bhandari accused protesters of vandalising the Hyderabad office. A party social media official told Reuters two accounts had been restored but thousands remain restricted. Police registered a complaint against four Youth Congress leaders in Mumbai. Meta had not commented on the allegations.
keyFacts: Protests were held at Meta offices in three Indian cities
Congress alleges accounts were restricted at the BJP's request
The BJP accused protesters of vandalism

leftOut.title: Economists forecast October inflation rise ahead of ABS release
leftOut.summary:
NAB economists forecast annual headline inflation will rise from 4.3 per cent to 4.7 per cent when the Australian Bureau of Statistics releases October consumer price figures on Wednesday, AAP reported. They said higher fuel costs and the card surcharge ban that began on 1 October were the main drivers.

NAB's Taylor Nugent said he expected October to be the peak. Treasurer Jim Chalmers told question time inflation would be higher than the government would like, citing oil prices in October, according to AAP. The official figures had not been released at the time of the report.
keyFacts: NAB forecasts 4.7% annual headline inflation
ABS releases October figures on Wednesday
Chalmers says inflation will be higher than wanted

leftOut.title: Melanoma researcher Georgina Long named joint winner of Prime Minister's Prize for Science
leftOut.summary:
Professor Georgina Long, medical director of Melanoma Institute Australia, was named co-recipient of the 2026 Prime Minister's Prize for Science on Tuesday night, AAP and the ABC reported. AAP said her work with the late Richard Scolyer helped lift survival from advanced melanoma above 50 per cent.

The prize was shared with subatomic physicist Anthony Thomas, according to AAP. Other awards went to Mark Smythe, Asha Bowen, Malcolm Macintosh and Chris Matthews. Long told AAP that teachers help make curiosity part of life.
keyFacts: Long is a joint winner of the top science prize
Prize shared with physicist Anthony Thomas
Awards announced on Tuesday night

leftOut.title: Two arrested after break-in at Prince William's Norfolk home
leftOut.summary:
Norfolk police said two men were arrested on suspicion of burglary and trespass at a property on the Sandringham estate after reports of suspicious activity on Monday night, AAP reported. The property, Anmer Hall, was unoccupied and the family was not present.

Police used dogs, drones and a helicopter in the search, according to AAP. The two men were in custody on Tuesday and had not been charged. The Sun newspaper first reported the break-in. Anmer Hall is used by the Prince and Princess of Wales mainly for holidays.
keyFacts: Two men arrested on suspicion of burglary
House was unoccupied at the time
No charges laid as of Tuesday

leftOut.title: Victorian business groups seek greater role with next state government
leftOut.summary:
Victorian business groups told AAP they want a greater say in decisions after Saturday's state election. Victorian Chamber of Commerce and Industry chief executive Sally Curtain said business had been locked out of key decisions and called for clarity on the COVID debt payroll levy.

Tim Piper of the Victorian Congress of Employer Associations said businesses wanted to work closely with the next government. At a radio leaders' forum on Tuesday, Premier Ben Carroll defended the state's debt, while Opposition Leader Jess Wilson pointed to $26 billion in planned savings, according to AAP.
keyFacts: Victorians vote on Saturday
Business groups seek more consultation
Coalition cites $26 billion in planned savings

leftOut.title: Jury to begin deliberations in Lamarre-Condon double murder trial
leftOut.summary:

Pacific island nations are turning to their own climate coalitions after the COP31 talks in Turkey ended without an agreement, AAP reported. Trump said Xi agreed with the concept, according to Reuters, while China has been reluctant to join arms control talks. Faye dismissed Sonko as prime minister in May 2026, and Sonko is now speaker of the National Assembly, according to Africanews and Channel Africa. Faye launched his own party in July. leftOut.summary:

Somalia accuses the UAE of violating its sovereignty and supporting armed forces outside federal control, according to AP. The UAE has ties with Somaliland, Puntland and Jubbaland. UAE adviser Anwar Gargash accused President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud of putting personal calculations first. Chairman John Moolenaar said the US and its allies should tighten export controls and investment restrictions.

The report names Honeywell, GE Aerospace and Collins as having obtained licences for technology transfers involving Chinese military end users, the committee said. The report says China could escalate to a blockade or quarantine if its political approach fails, according to the newspaper. Eunews said Reuters reported Berlin would back the Spanish candidate if Markus Brunnermeier became chief economist. The day before, Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi said Japan's position was unchanged from the 1972 joint communique and called for stable ties with Beijing, according to Anadolu, citing Kyodo. Opponents said they would keep opposing the facility.

leftOut.summary:

Issues raised included the cost of living, climate, education budgets, housing, defence spending and compulsory military service, according to the ABC. The Berlin rally was among the largest. In Rome a small group threw firecrackers, but events were mostly peaceful, and London police kept a rival group apart from students. Organisers said larger Paris protests were planned for the weekend.

Irine Cheptai is set to be named champion, according to AAP. The Athletics Integrity Unit also announced bans for two other Kenyan runners. Vana-Reese Schuster-Togiatau was shot during a boxing event and died five days later, according to AAP. Three men were also injured. Rights groups say more than 1 per cent of the population has been detained under a state of emergency with limited due process, according to the report. AAP said about 5,000 Rohingya live in Australia. Her family stayed up on Thursday night to watch the ruling from The Hague, according to the report. leftOut.title: Carroll says Victorian election is winnable as poll shows Labor behind
leftOut.summary:
Victorian Premier Ben Carroll said every election is winnable ahead of the 28 November state poll, AAP reported. Carroll took over five months ago after a leadership spill that led to Jacinta Allan's resignation.

A RedBridge Group and Accent Research survey published in the Australian Financial Review put the Coalition on 31 per cent, Labor on 23 per cent and One Nation on 22 per cent, AAP said. Carroll is defending his seat of Niddrie, which he held in 2022 on a 6.7 per cent margin. He acknowledged Labor faced a difficult contest but said he would keep campaigning across the state.
keyFacts: The election is on 28 November
The RedBridge survey had Labor on 23% primary vote
Carroll is defending Niddrie on a 6.7% margin

leftOut.title: Kensington Palace announces documentary on Princess of Wales's cancer treatment
leftOut.summary:
Kensington Palace has announced a documentary, Heal, about the Princess of Wales's experience of cancer, the ABC reported, citing AFP and Reuters. It will air on the BBC on 29 November and on Channel Nine in Australia on 1 December.

The palace said the film follows her on the Three Peaks Challenge, which she completed in June, and features others facing serious illness. Catherine announced in March 2024 that she was being treated for cancer and said in January 2025 that she was in remission. The palace said funds from distribution will go to the Royal Marsden Cancer Charity.
keyFacts: The documentary airs on the BBC on 29 November
It screens on Channel Nine on 1 December
Proceeds go to the Royal Marsden Cancer Charity

leftOut.title: ABC analysis examines Albanese's diplomacy after APEC and Quad trip
leftOut.summary:
An ABC analysis by chief digital political correspondent Clare Armstrong reviews Prime Minister Anthony Albanese's 11-day trip, which included the Quad meeting in Manila and APEC in China. It notes that Albanese told Russian President Vladimir Putin at APEC to end the war in Ukraine, and that US President Donald Trump met Putin and Chinese President Xi Jinping in Shenzhen.

Armstrong argues Albanese has grown more comfortable managing relations with Beijing and Washington but has limited influence over decisions made by the three leaders. The piece is analysis and does not report new events beyond those already covered.
keyFacts: The trip lasted 11 days and included APEC and the Quad
Albanese urged Putin to end the war, the ABC said
The piece is analysis, not new reporting
